Fictional court opinion for software demonstrations; no real case is represented.

# Marsh Records Association v. Harbour Authority

## Facts

The association requested raw readings from water-level loggers used in a publicly
funded marsh project. The authority released a polished report but withheld the
underlying measurements, describing them as unfinished working material.

## Procedural history

The trial tribunal accepted the authority's explanation. The association appealed,
arguing that producing a report did not eliminate the separate duty to disclose
the observations on which it relied.

## Analysis

Under the fictional access rule assumed here, observations collected with public
funds remain records even when incomplete. A warning about failed sensors may
explain uncertainty; it does not transform recorded measurements into private
deliberation. The distinction is between observations and internal recommendations.

## Holding

The authority must disclose the recorded measurements and identify missing intervals.
It may attach an explanation of sensor failures. This decision does not require new
measurements, a new scientific analysis or release of protected staff deliberations.

## Disposition

The refusal is reversed and the matter returned for disclosure under the stated
conditions. The tribunal does not decide whether reopening channels benefits habitat.

## Dissent

The dissent would permit a short delay to validate timestamps, but agrees that a
published summary cannot permanently replace access to the underlying readings.
